_README: The text that actually reaches the app when a generation fails, for #403.
Every needle in RunFailureKind used to come from what a developer imagined
Python writes. These are measured instead. generate_week.py stores the bare
str(e) of the exception in errors[day], with no prefix of its own, so what is
recorded here is exactly what the classifier reads.
`provenance` on each entry says how it was obtained, and it is the whole point
of this file. Do not add an entry without one, and do not write `captured` on
something that was reasoned about (L48).
captured        run against the real thing on 2026-08-12, text copied verbatim
sdk-formatter   built by the line in the installed SDK that builds these
messages (_base_client.py, `Error code: {status} - {body}`),
with the API's documented error body. The `captured` 401 entry
below matches this construction exactly, character for
character, which is what makes it trustworthy for the statuses
that cannot be triggered on demand.
One entry is deliberately absent. A rate limit and an overload cannot be caused
to order, and the SDK is configured with max_retries=4, so by the time either
reaches the app it has already backed off four times. Both are recorded here as
sdk-formatter rather than pretended to be captured.
#522 completed the API half. The app has exactly ONE call site into the service,
claude_client, and it catches anthropic.APIError, which every SDK exception
including the transport ones inherits from. So the set of texts that can reach
the classifier from the service is closed, and every status in it is now here:
400, 401, 403, 413, 429, 500, 529, plus the two failures that carry no status at
all. The sdk-formatter entries were produced by handing the documented body for
each status to the installed SDK's own error constructor and taking str() of
what came back, so the wording is the SDK's rather than anyone's memory of it.
That closed set is what let the guard in test_failure_needles_have_producers.py
drop its marker split and start covering the whole classifier.

cases.note: Trying to cause this for real cost 0.72 USD and did not produce it: 240k tokens was accepted rather than refused, because the window is far larger than assumed. Not attempted again. Reducing inputs is the only thing that fixes it, so classifying it as a generic service error tells Dan to wait and retry something that will fail identically.

cases.name: the key is valid but not allowed to use this
cases.note: 403 is a different thing from 401: the key is real and the account cannot use what was asked for. It reaches authFailed on the words `API key`, which is the right place to send Dan, since both are fixed by looking at the key rather than by waiting.

cases.name: the service broke on its own
cases.note: 500 is transient in a way 400 and 413 are not, so waiting and retrying is the correct advice here and would be wrong for those.

cases.name: the request never reached the service
cases.note: A transport failure carries no HTTP status and no error body at all, so every status-code needle misses it and it is caught only by the words the client puts in front. Recorded because two needles, `apiconnectionerror` and `apistatuserror`, were written expecting the exception's CLASS name to appear here. It does not: claude_client raises `Anthropic API error: {e}`, and str() of an SDK exception is its message, never its type.

cases.name: the request timed out
cases.note: The other half of the no-status case. A long week batch is the realistic way to meet it.
cases.text: Anthropic API error: Request timed out or interrupted. This could be due to a network timeout, dropped connection, or request cancellation. See https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/errors#long-requests for more details.

cases.name: a reply with no text block in it
cases.note: Raised by claude_client itself rather than by the SDK, and it does not contain the words `api error`, so it used to fall through to the unrecognised fallback.
cases.text: Anthropic API returned no text block. Blocks received: thinking

cases.name: a crash in our own code
cases.note: Must stay unknown. Nothing may be claimed about a failure we do not recognise, and the raw text is shown on its own.

cases.name: a model id the service does not have
cases.note: Reached by postroll/ai/model_ids.py going stale after a deprecation, which is rare but real. A 404 carries no needle of its own, so it fell through to the generic service branch and Dan was told the service was having trouble and to wait a minute. Retrying a model the service does not have fails identically forever, which is the same defect #403 fixed for 413 and for a prompt past the context window: a permanent failure wearing a transient one's advice.
cases.text: Anthropic API error: Error code: 404 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'not_found_error', 'message': 'model: claude-opus-9'}, 'request_id': 'req_011CTgLm4rB29WqSaMPLE'}

cases.name: the Python checkout is not where the app looked
cases.note: Captured on 2026-08-17 for #648 by running the exact script shape PythonBridge.runProcess builds, with the project root pointed at the folder the app used to hardcode. Two things make this the ONLY text the classifier sees: the shell's `cd` failure goes to the stderr pipe Swift reads, while Python's own error goes to the run's private log, and ProcessRunner consults that log only when the pipe is EMPTY. It is not empty, it holds this one line. Before this kind existed the line matched the generic `no such file` needle and came back as fileMissing, whose sentence tells Dan to re-assign his photos. His photos were never involved, and no amount of re-assigning them could have fixed it.
